summary: In Greek mythology, Thersanon (also Thersanor; Ancient Greek Θερσάνων) was an Argonaut from Andros, son of Helios and Leucothoe. Hyginus places him in the Argo's crew beside other sons of the Sun; the mother's identity is debated against Ovid's Babylonian Leucothoe, who dies transformed into frankincense.

sections.heading: Argonaut from Andros
paragraphs: Hyginus (Fabulae 14) lists Thersanon son of the Sun and Leucothoe among the Argonauts sailing from Andros. As a child of Helios he is paternal half-brother to Aeëtes of Colchis, keeper of the Fleece the crew seeks. The Fabulae text is corrupt; editors restore Thersanon or Thersanor (the latter also appears in an alphabetic Argonaut list on papyrus).

sections.heading: Leucothoe problem
paragraphs: Ovid's Leucothoe is a Babylonian princess Helios loves; her father buries her alive and the god turns her body into a frankincense tree — a story that leaves little room for a surviving son. Hyginus' parentage may imply another Leucothoe (or Leucothea), a different local version in which she lives long enough to bear a child, or a simple handbook conflation. The atlas keeps thersanon-andros as Hyginus' Andrian Argonaut.
